use_case_name: Copy Uncompressed Files to Another Location

claims.content: To copy one or more files or folders from a source location to a destination location without compressing them.

goal.raw_text: To copy one or more files or folders from a source location to a destination location without compressing them.

claims.content: User
The user has launched the PeaZip application.
The user is viewing the File Manager Interface or a specific archive content view within PeaZip.
The source files or folders to be copied are visible and accessible within the current PeaZip window.
The destination location (folder) where the files will be copied exists and is accessible via the computer system's file structure or another open PeaZip window.

The user selects one or more files or folders within the PeaZip interface and initiates a copy action, typically by pressing the 'Copy' button on the toolbar, selecting 'Copy' from the context menu, or using the Ctrl+C keyboard shortcut.

trigger.raw_text: The user selects one or more files or folders within the PeaZip interface and initiates a copy action, typically by pressing the 'Copy' button on the toolbar, selecting 'Copy' from the context menu, or using the Ctrl+C keyboard shortcut.

claims.content: The user selects the file(s) or folder(s) they wish to copy within the PeaZip interface.
The user initiates the copy command (e.g., via toolbar button, context menu, or keyboard shortcut).
PeaZip copies the selected items to the system clipboard.
The user navigates to the destination folder where the files are to be pasted.
The user initiates the paste command (e.g., via toolbar button, context menu, or keyboard shortcut).
PeaZip retrieves the items from the clipboard and writes them to the destination location on the storage device.
PeaZip displays a progress indicator if the operation takes time, and confirms completion once the files are successfully copied.

If the destination folder contains files with the same names as the files being copied, PeaZip may prompt the user to choose an action (e.g., overwrite, skip, or rename) depending on the application settings configured in the Settings Interface.
If the user attempts to copy files to a location where they do not have write permissions, PeaZip will display an error message indicating that the operation failed due to access restrictions.

If the source files are located within a compressed archive and the user attempts to copy them using drag-and-drop instead of the standard copy/paste commands, PeaZip will automatically extract the files to the temporary folder or the drop target location before completing the copy operation.

If the computer system lacks the required x-86 compatible CPU architecture necessary for PeaZip's performance-critical sections written in ASM, the application may fail to execute the copy function or run correctly.

If the source files are encrypted ('locked') and the user has not provided the correct password or keyfile via the authentication interface, PeaZip will prevent the copying/accessing of the file contents, adhering to security requirements.
If the storage device runs out of space during the write operation at the destination location, the copy process will terminate, and PeaZip will display an error message indicating the failure.
If the source files are corrupted or contain bad sectors that prevent reading, PeaZip will halt the operation and notify the user of the read error.

In the event of any unexpected error (such as wrong data insertion or internal logic failure), PeaZip is required to provide the user with an appropriate help message explaining the issue before exiting the specific operation flow.
